findings.title: Title Screen Obscurity
findings.where: Title Screen, background image and central vehicle models
findings.problem: The background render is heavily crushed, muddy, and desaturated. While the intent is a moody sunset, the foreground vehicles are merely silhouettes and the background city is lost in the gloom.
findings.why: As the first thing the player sees, it obscures the art direction and fails to showcase the vehicle models which are the core asset of the game.
findings.fix: Increase the key light intensity on the foreground vehicles and boost saturation on the horizon. Use a lighter, cleaner vignette overlay so the cars remain the focal point.

findings.title: City Value Flattening
findings.where: City Screen, the ground and building models
findings.problem: The environment palette is almost entirely monochromatic blue-grey. The buildings, the road, and the cracked ground terrain share the exact same brightness value and color.
findings.why: This creates a 'grey soup' effect where it is difficult to distinguish buildings from flat street debris, hurting depth perception and wayfinding.
findings.fix: Separate the values: darken the ground texture and significantly brighten or shift the hue of the building materials. Add hard shadows to emphasize height.

findings.title: Road Texture Ambiguity
findings.problem: The asphalt texture is low-contrast grey static noise that blends too closely with the off-road pavement. There is very little vertical contrast to separate the road from the wreckage/terrain.
findings.why: At speed, the player needs instant confirmation of the drivable lane. Currently, the visual hierarchy between 'danger/debris' and 'road' is weak, which adds friction to combat driving.
findings.fix: Increase the contrast of the lane markers (make yellow brighter/whiter) and slightly desaturate/darken the asphalt texture to visually separate it from the lighter, broken ground surrounding it.

findings.title: Arena Floor Definition
findings.problem: The 'Practice Arena' floor is essentially a flat, beige noise texture. It lacks the visual cues of a man-made structure—no concrete pattern, no wall bases, no distinct floor color.
findings.why: It feels like an empty dirt patch or a missing texture rather than a constructed competitive space. It lacks the visual weight required to feel like a 'stage' for combat.
findings.fix: Replace the noise texture with a structured pattern (like a concrete grid or cross-hatching) and add a distinct, slightly brighter border line to define the arena boundaries.

findings.title: Constructor UI Legibility
findings.where: Constructor Screen, the component list on the left
findings.problem: The list of components (Weapon 1 through Weapon 10) uses thin, small grey text on a dark blue background. The list is incredibly dense with no whitespace or grouping.
findings.why: The 'readability at a glance' is low. Players scanning for stats or configuration options will find this fatiguing and slow to parse compared to the high-speed action of the game.
findings.fix: Switch to a bolder font weight, increase text brightness to white or light grey, and add alternating row colors or distinct visual separators for every 3-4 weapon slots to break up the list.
